messages:
Lee (customer): Hey team — hitting a build error when adding the Node TS SDK to our Next.js app. Dev build fails with: `Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports"` after upgrading to `redwood-node-sdk@2.0.0`.

Lee (customer): Minimal error log: ```
> next build
Error: Cannot find module 'redwood-node-sdk'
Caused by: ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './package.json' is not defined by "exports" in /node_modules/redwood-node-sdk/package.json
```

Lee (customer): Our package.json for the app includes standard Next setup. I inspected the SDK package.json and its exports section looks like: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js" },
  "./package.json": "package.json"
}
```

Sara (support): thanks for the report, lee. do you have the full app repro or a small example? quick questions: node version, next version, and which bundler (next usually uses webpack; are you using custom esbuild config)? also did you install via npm or yarn/pnpm?

Lee (customer): Node v18.16, Next 13.4, npm. I tried both `npm i` and `pnpm i` (different CI) — same error in Vercel build and locally. I put a tiny repro here: https://gist.github.com/lee-org/abc123 (contains package.json + next.config.js)

Mike (devex): copying some common causes: 1) bundlers can choke when package exposes `./package.json` in exports — some bundler resolution algos try to import package.json and can't if it's not exported. 2) mixed ESM/CJS artifacts where consumers expect `main` or a CJS path. 3) TypeScript consumers sometimes import types via `types` entry that doesn't exist in distributed tarball.

Mike (devex): quick workaround to unblock: in next.config.js add a webpack alias pointing to the CJS bundle: ```js
module.exports = {
  webpack: (config) => {
    config.resolve.alias['redwood-node-sdk'] = path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-node-sdk/dist/index.cjs.js')
    return config
  }
}
```

Sara (support): another quick check: can you run `npm pack` in the app after installing the SDK and then `tar -tf` the .tgz to confirm dist files + types are present? sometimes publish step omitted `.d.ts` files. also please paste `node -p "require('node:module').createRequire(require.resolve('redwood-node-sdk'))"` output if possible.

Lee (customer): ran `npm pack` — dist has `index.mjs`, `index.cjs.js`, but no `index.d.ts`. package.json `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts`. so types path is missing.

Tyler (packaging): hey — packaging lead here. we recently tightened the `exports` map to be explicit and dropped a legacy `./package.json` export to reduce accidental json imports. apparently that caused some bundlers to fail for CJS consumers. also looks like a publishing bug clipped `dist/index.d.ts` from the tarball in 2.0.0.

Tyler (packaging): immediate plan: publish 2.0.1 that restores a compatible exports map and includes missing types. will also add a `browser` field and ensure a `main` fallback for older bundlers.

Lee (customer): appreciate it. any ETA? build is blocking our deploy today.

Tyler (packaging): aiming for a patch release within 2 hours. will post release notes and the exact change. in the meantime, please use workaround: pin `redwood-node-sdk@1.9.4` or add the webpack alias above.

Sara (support): for our internal tracking, please attach the gist link and CI build logs to the support ticket. I'll mark this as P1 until the patch lands. also note that Vercel builds may cache the node_modules; clearing build cache after pin/patch is necessary. :+1:

Lee (customer): pinned to 1.9.4, local build succeeded. thanks, that unblocks us. will hold off on deploy until patch is in prod.

Mike (devex): postmortem notes for packaging: when you restore exports please include both `import`/`require` and `types` entries and consider adding `"exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }}` so TS-aware tools resolve properly. also add a `files` entry in package.json to ensure d.ts ends up in the tarball.

Tyler (packaging): noted. I'll run `npm pack` locally on the candidate 2.0.1 and paste the `tar -tf` output here before publishing. once published, deploy-bot will trigger a canary rollout.

deploy-bot: Patch release 2.0.1 scheduled — tests running.

Tyler (packaging): uploaded 2.0.1 to npm and verified artifacts include `dist/index.cjs.js`, `dist/index.mjs`, and `dist/index.d.ts`. exports map restored to include require/import/types and `./package.json` entry to support older resolvers.

Sara (support): @lee once npm registry replicates, please upgrade to 2.0.1 and confirm your Vercel build. if anything still fails, we'll reopen and request a minimal repro repo.

Lee (customer): upgraded and deployed — build OK, tests pass, site live. thanks everyone! :rocket:

Sara (support): closing thread — root cause: packaging/publish regression (exports + missing d.ts) introduced in 2.0.0. mitigation: patch 2.0.1, temporary pin to 1.9.4 or add webpack alias. action items: packaging to add CI `npm pack` artifact check and devex to add a short checklist for publishing SDKs.

Tyler (packaging): will open GH issue with checklist and assign. ETA for CI check: next sprint.

Mike (devex): adding a short doc snippet to SDK publishing guide about `exports` + `types` checks.

Lee (customer): thanks again, team.
